subject: Materials Science
title: Power Semiconductors: Handling Big Current
description: A fast breakdown of Power Semiconductors: Handling Big Current for builders.

hook.text: A tiny silicon chip switches 1,000 amps in an electric train — power semiconductors move the world.

buildup.text: IGBTs and power MOSFETs handle high voltage and current — they're the muscles of power electronics.

discovery.text: Thick, lightly doped drift regions withstand high voltage — but resistance and switching losses are the trade-off.

twist.text: Silicon carbide (SiC) handles three times the voltage of silicon in the same thickness — revolutionizing EV inverters.

climax.text: Tesla's Model 3 switched from silicon to SiC MOSFETs — gaining 5% more range from the same battery.

punchline.text: Small chips controlling big power — that's how electricity gets to work.

quiz.question: Why is silicon carbide replacing silicon in power electronics?
options: SiC handles higher voltages with lower losses in the same chip size
